faq.title: Asked before the first month is closed

items.q: Is a dormant client still an open file?
items.a: Only if you leave it open. Archiving a client keeps every posting and every document readable for as long as your plan keeps closed years, and it stops counting towards the limit on the day you archive it.
One document that arrives to be matched against a posting: a supplier invoice, a till slip, a fuel docket. A bank line is not a receipt, and a document you upload twice is counted once.

items.q: Can we move a plan in the middle of the year?
items.a: Moving up takes effect the moment you confirm it and you pay the difference for the days left. Moving down takes effect on the renewal date, so the month you are closing is never disturbed.

items.q: What happens to the books if we leave?
items.a: Everything exports as spreadsheets and PDFs, ledger by ledger and client by client, and the export stays available for ninety days after the last billing day. Nothing is held back while an invoice is disputed.

items.q: Do you take a cut of what we bill our clients?
items.a: No. Daftar charges the practice and nothing else. What you charge a client for keeping their books is between the two of you and never passes through us.

cta.title: Close one client month and see how it reads
cta.lead: Every plan opens with a 30-day trial on the whole ledger. No card to start, nothing charged before the trial ends, and the file you build during it is the file you keep.
